steps.tx: **Hyperacute rejection** occurs within minutes of vascular clamp release, mediated by **pre-existing antibodies** against donor ABO or HLA class **1** antigens that activate complement, triggering widespread **thrombotic occlusion** and graft necrosis. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

steps.tx: The **Banff classification** grades **TCMR** by interstitial inflammation and **tubulitis**: Grade IA displays i2/i3 with t2; Grade IB displays i2/i3 with t3; Grade II displays **intimal arteritis** with v1/v2; and Grade III displays transmural arteritis with v3. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

steps.tx: Acute **antibody-mediated rejection** requires three **Banff criteria**: histological tissue injury with glomerulitis and **peritubular capillaritis**, evidence of recent antibody action with **C4d** in at least **10%** of capillaries, and circulating **DSA**. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

vis.caption: Tubulitis, intimal arteritis, and peritubular capillaritis. Capillaritis is one of the tissue-injury lesions in antibody-mediated rejection. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: First-line therapy for **acute cellular rejection** is intravenous **methylprednisolone** at **500** mg daily for **3** days, escalating to lymphocyte-depleting rabbit antithymocyte globulin, or **rATG**, for steroid-resistant or Banff Grade II/III vascular rejection. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

nodes.label: Confirm Banff TCMR on allograft biopsy
Pulse methylprednisolone 500 mg IV x 3 days

edges: Persistent allograft dysfunction at 5 to 7 days

steps.tx: **Acute antibody-mediated rejection** is treated with multimodal therapy including therapeutic **plasma exchange** (PEX) to remove circulating DSA, intravenous immunoglobulin, or **IVIG**, and anti-CD**20** monoclonal antibody **rituximab** or proteasome inhibitor bortezomib. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

left.title: Antibody Removal
points: Modality: Therapeutic plasma exchange (5 to 7 sessions)
Target: Physical removal of circulating donor-specific anti-HLA IgG
Monitoring: Serial SAB Luminex DSA MFI tracking
Replacement: 5% albumin with fresh frozen plasma finishing

right.title: Immunomodulation
points: IVIg: Low-dose post-PEX (100 to 200 mg/kg) or high-dose (2 g/kg)
Rituximab: Single dose (375 mg/m2) to deplete CD20+ B cells
Bortezomib: Proteasome inhibitor targeting mature plasma cells
Tocilizumab: Anti-IL6 receptor blocker for chronic active AMR

steps.tx: **Chronic active AMR** represents the leading cause of late allograft loss. Biopsy demonstrates **transplant glomerulopathy** with a cg score > **0**, showing basement membrane **double contours** and extensive peritubular capillary basement membrane multilayering. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.
steps.say: Chronic active AMR represents the leading cause of late allograft loss. Biopsy demonstrates transplant glomerulopathy with a cg score exceeding 0, showing basement membrane double contours and extensive peritubular capillary basement membrane multilayering. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

rows: Progressive proteinuria and refractory allograft loss
Hallmark of repetitive endothelial microvascular injury

steps.tx: **Donor-derived cell-free DNA**, or **dd-cfDNA**, serves as a non-invasive **liquid biopsy** **biomarker**. A dd-cfDNA fraction exceeding **0.5%** to **1.0%** accurately differentiates acute allograft rejection from calcineurin inhibitor toxicity and stable graft function. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

rows: Treat with oral corticosteroid pulse and taper
Optimize maintenance immunosuppression and monitor DSA

steps.tx: **Interstitial fibrosis** and **tubular atrophy**, abbreviated as **IFTA**, on protocol allograft biopsy reflects chronic **cumulative damage** from immune rejection, chronic calcineurin inhibitor nephrotoxicity, hypertension, and recurrent viral infections. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients. Structured clinical management and regular follow-up help guide therapeutic optimization and prevent disease complications.
